newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stock rally notches up another point.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stock rally notches up another point.

text.p: Strong buying by foreign funds and local institutional investors drove up Chilean blue chips another full point as a New Year's rally began to look on increasingly solid footing, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index closed 1.05 percent higher at 112.13 points. The all-share IGPA ended 0.72 percent higher at 5263.93 points.
Brokers pointed to good volume of 14.6 billion pesos, the highest level this week, as a sign the bourse's 12-point rally this year was starting to look more like a true realignment and not a fluke.
''We're starting to see some real consistency to this. Volume is not bad and there's optimism,'' said one broker.
He and other brokers said prices were likely to fall early Thursday in a technical retreat but then climb back up, a pattern often repeated in the past two weeks.
With Wednesday's 12-point rise, the IPSA has recovered in nominal terms all the ground it lost in 1996, although in real terms the index fell 17 percent.
Gainers included Edelnor, up 1.7 percent to 173 pesos. It announced it will buy into the Atacama natural gas pipeline. Other electricals also gained, including Endesa, up 1.4 percent to 250 pesos.
Maderas y Sinteticos, planning a capital increase early this year to finance Brazilian investments, rose 3.6 percent to 230 pesos. Santander Chile BSB.Nu was up 3.2 percent to 32 pesos.
The market also noted Mexico's early repayment of part of its U.S. bailout but brokers said the move had no direct impact on Chilean shares.
Lord Cochrane was up 7.6 percent to 85 pesos on news reports of stronger 1997 earnings.
Decliners included Colbun, off 1.6 percent to 31.50 pesos, and Andina, down 1.6 percent to 2165 pesos.
